title: Tuning and evaluating a random forest regressor

items.stem: Definitions: In a random forest regressor, what does the max_features setting control?

options.text: The number of features each tree is trained on, chosen once per tree
The number of features kept after dropping the least important ones
The number of features randomly drawn as split candidates at each split
The maximum number of features allowed along one root-to-leaf path

items.stem: Definitions: In one phrase, what does the min_samples_leaf setting of a regression tree fix?
Definitions: Which of these best defines the out-of-bag (OOB) score of a random forest regressor?

options.text: Prediction error on each row, using only trees whose bootstrap sample excluded that row
Training error of each tree, averaged over the rows that tree was grown on
Error on a held-out test set that the forest never saw during fitting
Error on the rows that a validation split set aside before the forest was fitted

items.stem: Definitions: Which statement about the n_estimators setting of a random forest regressor is correct?

options.text: It is the number of bootstrap rows drawn to train each single tree
It is the number of candidate split points tried at each node
It is the number of random row subsets each tree is validated on
It is how many separate trees are fitted and then averaged to predict

items.stem: Definitions: Which statement correctly describes the RMSE of a regression model?

options.text: The share of the target's variance that the model explains, on a scale up to 1
A typical size of the prediction errors, in the target's units, where large misses count extra
The average absolute size of the prediction errors, in the target's units, with every miss counted equally
The square of the average prediction error, so that over- and under-predictions cancel out

items.stem: Applying it: A forest of 100 trees with max_features=0.5 and min_samples_leaf=1 is fitted to 50,000 rows with the OOB score switched on. It reaches a training R² of 0.98 and an OOB R² of 0.71. Which change is most likely to raise the OOB R²?

options.text: Raise n_estimators from 100 to 1,000 so averaging more trees removes most of the variance
Raise min_samples_leaf from 1 to 10 so each tree fits less noise
Raise max_features from 0.5 to 1.0 so each split can always pick the strongest feature
Remove any depth limit so each tree can grow until every leaf is pure

items.stem: Applying it: At one input, each of the 100 trees in a forest has prediction variance 4. The predictions of any two different trees have correlation 0.5. What is the variance of the forest's averaged prediction at that input?

Applying it: An analyst tries 60 combinations of settings, picks the one with the best R² on the test set, and reports that test R² as the expected performance on new data. How does that figure compare with the model's true performance on new data?

options.text: Likely too high: the 60 tries were ranked on these same rows, so the winner partly fits their quirks
Likely too low: the forest never trained on the test rows, so it has not seen them
About right: a forest averages many trees, so choosing settings on the test set cannot bias its score
About right: R² is computed from predictions only, so how the settings were chosen does not matter

items.stem: Applying it: A tuned forest predicts house prices. On four validation rows, its errors (predicted minus actual) are +1, -2, +2 and -4 thousand dollars. What is its RMSE on these rows, in thousand dollars?

Applying it: A soccer analytics team fits forests to predict expected goals from shot data. The OOB R² is 0.80 with 25 trees, 0.868 with 100 trees, 0.872 with 400 trees and 0.873 with 1,600 trees. Training cost grows in proportion to the number of trees. The team accepts the cheapest forest whose OOB R² is within 0.002 of the best score listed. Which number of trees should it use?

options.text: 25, because it is the cheapest to train and already scores 0.80
100, because most of the total gain has already arrived by that point
400, because it is the cheapest forest within 0.002 of the best score
1,600, because it has the highest OOB R² of all the forests
